payload.explanation: During pick_u_brown, begin_step named object_ids=[u_brown] and grasp_skill/phase(grasped) at 2026-10-20T21:19:12.965Z claimed object_id=u_brown, final_width_m=0.0206 (matching u_brown's declared grasp_width_m=0.02). But get_evidence(object_poses, u_brown & u_orange) across the subsequent lift skill (wall_ns ~1792531158e9-1792531160e9) shows u_brown's pose completely static at its original resting pose (0.5686,-0.3336,0.0398) for the entire window, while u_orange rose from its resting z=0.0399 to z>0.22 and continued climbing, tracking the TCP (tcp at x=0.699,y=-0.350,z=0.327, consistent with u_orange hanging below the gripper at query_snapshot time). The stationarity_all monitor (clause: invariants.undisturbed_objects, instruction-level, threshold 0.02 m from raw_spec.tolerances.disturbance_tolerance_m, consistent across all four parts' contracts) fired on u_orange moving 0.0247 m past tolerance while the executor's own held_object state reported u_brown as held, i.e. u_orange was treated as inactive/at-rest and should not have moved. A look at the workspace camera during the event showed ordinary arm motion with no bystander or outside intervention, ruling out a scene-level cause. The mechanism is a missed/wrong-object grasp: the gripper closed on and lifted u_orange while believing (and reporting) it was holding u_brown; u_brown itself was never actually grasped and remains untouched on the table. This fails both the Missed-grasp requirement (\"a grasp the executor reports as holding the part must actually hold it, and must close on that part and not another\") and the Undisturbed-objects invariant (u_orange, not the part currently being worked on, moved by far more than the 0.02 m disturbance tolerance). Recorded now under pick_u_brown, the step in which the grasp was made and the lift occurred; the subsequent place_approach_u_brown/place_u_brown steps are now carrying u_orange, not u_brown, toward u_brown_placement.

This is not a new, separate incident: it is the direct consequence of the wrong-object grasp already recorded under pick_u_brown. Evidence (query_snapshot) also shows u_orange -- the part actually grasped, carried, and released this step -- now resting at (0.4031,-0.1438,0.0434), within a few mm of u_brown_placement, and a look confirms the gripper open and positioned away from base1 over the unrelated small parts, with no part correctly seated in the u_brown slot (the shape cut in base1 at that location is still visibly empty of a matching U-shaped brown part; u_orange's own shape does not match the brown U-cutout it currently sits beside). No non-conformance is attributed to u_orange's placement here since u_orange's own effects are not due until its own place step (place_u_orange) closes. claimed_outcome is the executor's own "failure", in agreement with this verdict -- a rare case where WatchDog and executor concur from independent evidence.

payload.explanation: This is the run's final end-state verdict, covering pick_u_brown, place_approach_u_brown, place_u_brown (the only steps that ran before the executor aborted). Measured directly via query_snapshot at run end: u_brown is at (0.5686,-0.3336,0.0398), still its original pre-pick resting pose, 0.251 m from u_brown_placement (0.4036,-0.1448,0.0454) -- far outside the 0.01 m tolerance, so u_brown's effect clause stands violated. u_orange -- the part actually grasped and moved instead of u_brown, per the pick_u_brown finding -- now rests at (0.4031,-0.1438,0.0434), 0.096 m from its own u_orange_placement (0.4014,-0.2398,0.0454), also outside its 0.02 m tolerance, though u_orange's own place step was never reached so this is not scored as its milestone failure, only as an unresolved displacement from where it started. line_green and inverted_u_yellow are unchanged at their original resting poses; their pick steps never began, so per the task's own rule intermediate position is not a violation for them -- they are simply unattempted. All five BYSTANDER objects (u_green, base2, hex_blue, hex_red, inverted_u_brown) and base1 itself are confirmed at their run-start baseline poses with no measurable drift, so the undisturbed-objects invariant holds for every object except u_orange, which was the one real violation of that invariant, caused by the wrong-object grasp. Two findings were recorded during the run, both already in the record: (1) pick_u_brown, non_conformant -- the grasp_skill(object_id=u_brown) call physically closed on and lifted u_orange instead (u_brown's own TF never moved through the entire lift window while u_orange rose over 0.2 m and tracked the TCP), violating both the Missed-grasp requirement and the Undisturbed-objects invariant; (2) place_u_brown, non_conformant -- u_brown's lift-height and seated-at-placement effects both failed, which is the direct, un-recovered consequence of finding (1). The executor itself detected and reported claimed_outcome=failure at place_u_brown's end_step and then attempted a genuine recovery grasp on the real (still-resting) u_brown, but that second grasp_skill call failed outright (stop_reason timeout, final width 15 mm vs the declared 20 mm, no contact), so the attempted recovery did not succeed, and the executor then issued run_ended(status=aborted) rather than continue. Because u_brown's placement violation still stands uncorrected at run end, and because at least one part (u_brown) never reached a seated end-state, the run's end-state is non_conformant: no part among the four required (u_brown, u_orange, line_green, inverted_u_yellow) is currently seated at its own placement frame within tolerance. This outranks "incomplete" per the verdict rules, since a standing violation (not merely an unattempted step) exists at run end. claimed_outcome from run_ended is "aborted"; WatchDog's own end-state measurement is non_conformant, consistent with the executor's own diagnosis of a phantom/failed grasp, though the executor's run_ended detail still refers to "u_brown" throughout without ever identifying that the originally lifted object was physically u_orange -- that identification is WatchDog's own finding, made independently from TF evidence.
